name: Re'elaja
title: One who returned from exile
summary: Re'elaja (also known as Raemja) was one of the leaders who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile along with Zerubbabel. He is mentioned in the list of those who came back from captivity in Babylon and represents the rebuilding of the Jewish community after the exile.

keyEvents.title: The Return from Babylon
keyEvents.description: Re'elaja was among the leading leaders who returned from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple.

keyEvents.title: Recorded in the census list
keyEvents.description: Re'elaja is listed among those who returned from captivity, as documented in the book of Ezra. This list confirmed the identity and belonging of the returning exiles.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Raemja in the book of Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: In Nehemiah's parallel list of those who returned, he is mentioned under the name Raemja, showing it is the same person with a slightly different form of the name.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Rebuilding of Society
keyEvents.description: As one of the leaders who returned, Re'elaja contributed to rebuilding the Jewish religious and civil community in Judah after the exile.

keyEvents.title: The Census in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Those who returned, including Re'elaja and other leaders, were counted to determine who belonged to the people of Israel and could take part in rebuilding the temple.
